newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
DIFFERENCES OUTWEIGH MUTUAL GOALS: JIANG
India and China have resolved to address outstanding bilateral problems in a constructive spirit.

Setting the tone for talks, visiting Chinese President Jiang Zemin said the two countries' common interests far outweighed their differences at a banquet hosted by his Indian counterpart S D Sharma in the capital.

Sharma said India was willing to continue working with China to resolve the boundary question. He called for joint efforts to find a fair and mutually acceptable settlement within the framework of national interests and sentiments of the people of the two countries.

In an allusive reference to China's military and nuclear cooperation with Pakistan, Sharma said New Delhi was keen on building friendship with its neighbours and was concerned about developments affecting the security environment in the region.
The Economic Times
HFCL, SHINAWATRA IN MANAGEMENT SWAP
Himachal Futuristic Communications Ltd (HFCL) and Thailand based Shinawatra International Public Company have swapped management control of their joint ventures (JV) for cellular and paging services.
Shinawatra and HFCL are JV partners in three companies -- Microwave Communications Ltd (MCL) for paging services, Fascel Ltd for cellular services and HB Telecom (HBT) for basic services.
The swap in management is with regard to MCL and Fascel, where the Thai company had control of MCL, and the Indian one that of Fascel. Now, HFCL controls MCL and Shinawatra, Fascel.
The reversal in roles follows the sale of 30 percent of HFCL's stake in the cellular services company to the Hindujas and three percent to Shinawatra.
BOMBAY DYEING NET PLUNGES 78 PCT
The net profit of Bombay Dyeing and Manufacturing Co Ltd has plunged almost five times (78.25 percent) to 223.5 million rupees during April-September 1996 (1.02 billion rupees).

The net sales during the six months have dipped to 4.57 billion rupees against 7.27 billion rupees recorded in the last corresponding period. The fall in Bombay Dyeing's turnover and profitability was caused by a severe downward pressure on the international prices of DMT and PTA.
SIMPLER PASSBOOK SCHEME FOR EXPORTERS SOON
The commerce ministry is making a last ditch effort to reverse the trend of falling export growth by simplifying the passbook scheme as a sop to exporters.
The ministry is expected to make changes in the existing scheme to offer the exporters the facility to claim, as credit, a fixed percentage on the value of the imported raw materials.

The move is in response to numerous representations from exporter organisations pointing out that the Central Board of Excise and Customs insisted on end-use certificates before making any entries in the passbook.
ADB BLOWS ITS FUNDS IN THE WIND

More than half the loan from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for renewable energy development has been allocated by the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) for wind sources. The ADB has approved a $100-million loan to IREDA.

IREDA is under the ministry for non-conventional energy sources. The ADB loan is being used for the Renewable Energy Development Project. Based on its targets, IREDA has allocated the funds for the various non-conventional sources.
It plans to install 35 MW at an estimated cost of $60 million, the prime minister said in parliament.
STATE BANK POSTS 6.41 BLN RUPEES NET PROFIT

The State Bank of India (SBI) announced a net profit of 6.41 billion rupees for the first half of the fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). The SBI allotted 10.66 billion rupees for provisions and contingencies.

SBI chairman P G Kakodkar said the rise in net, higher than the 2.3 billion rupees net for the corresponding period last year, was mainly on account of a 21 percent increase in average performing loans and a lower provision on investment depreciation due to softening of interest rates this year.
The profit before provisions and contingencies was 17.07 billion rupees for the half year compared to 11.03 billion rupees in the corresponding period last year.
CENTRE MAY STEEL RINL BY CONVERTING LOAN INTO EQUITY
The Cabinet is considering the steel ministry's proposal to convert a part of the government's 35 billion rupee loan to state owned Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd (RINL) into equity.

The steel ministry plans to convert the loan given by the Union government to RINL either into equity share or preference shares. This is a part of RINL's capital restructuring plan, currently awaiting Cabinet clearance.
RINL, the holding company of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, has paid-up equity capital of over 57 billion rupees and a debt component of 35 billion rupees, most of which is owed to the government.
ARVIND MAFATLAL MAY CRY OFF DAHEJ PROJECT
The Arvind Mafatlal Group (AMG) is likely to pull out of the 5.5 billion rupee chemical port terminal project at Dahej in Maharashtra.

The only private sector participant in the seven-member promoter consortia, AMG, had proposed to route its investments through Gujarat Gas Company Ltd (GGCL), in which Mafatlal is joint venture partner.

GGCL had earlier agreed to take a five percent stake in the port company--Gujarat Chemical Port Terminal Ltd. According to sources, GGCL wanted to participate in the chemical port terminal only if GGCL was allowed to avail of the facility.
Financial Express
STEEL MAJOR POSTS 16.6 PCT FALL IN PROFIT

The introduction of minimum alternate tax reduced Steel Authority of India Ltd's (SAIL) post-tax profit by as much as 16.63 percent to only 3.61 billion rupees in the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).

SAIL's post-tax profit stood at 4.33 billion rupees during the same period last year. With the company's paid-up equity capital at 41.3 billion rupees from last year's level of 39.86 billion rupees, earnings per share plunged to 0.88 rupee from 1.09 rupees at the end of April-September period last year.
PROFIT OF 1,335 COMPANIES GOOD

The combined results of a select 1,335 companies indicated good performance during fiscal 1995/96 (April-March) in terms of sales and profits, according to a central bank (RBI) report on financial performance of private corporate business sector.

The sales of 1,335 companies grew by 26.2 percent in 1995/96 to 1639.67 billion rupees (1299.25 billion rupees in 1994/95). On the other hand, other income showed a moderate rise of 6.1 percent during 1995/96 and stood at 47.60 billion rupees. Total income thus recorded a rise of 25.5 percent.
TATA ELECTRIC'S NET DIPS TO 1.75 BLN RUPEE
The Tata Electric Companies (TEC) reported a 26 percent decline in net profit to 1.74 billion rupees for the half-year ended September 1996 due to high tax provisions and stagnant sales growth.

TEC is the umbrella organisation for the three power companies -- Tata Power, Tata Hydro and Andhra Valley. TEC's profit fell from the previous period's 2.37 billion rupees largely because of the stiff tax provision of 1.04 billion rupees. Sales growth was sluggish at 1.69 percent, rising to 11.81 billion rupees from 11.61 billion rupees in the same period last year.
APEX BANK FOR BODY TO OVERSEE BULLION TRADE
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, recommended setting up a gold management board with statutory powers to oversee wholesale bullion operations in the country.
The proposed board should examine and take steps to upgrade the standard and quality of the refineries in the country, RBI Deputy Governor Y.V. Reddy said.

The central bank also recommended introduction of hallmarking of gold jewellery as a measure of consumer protection. Besides, it suggested formulating an integrated national policy on gold covering trading, import, jewellery export, investment and refining.
ACC-CRA TO VENTURE INTO GOLD MINING

ACC-CRA Exploration Ltd, a joint venture between Associated Cement Companies (ACC) and CRA Ltd of Australia will begin prospecting for precious metals in India in the next six months, said ACC-CRA chairman Subrato Ganguly. ACC-CRA is the first firm approved by the Government after the new guidelines on private entry into mining came into effect.
Business Standard
FFR 376 MLN ON OFFER FOR SELECT CORE PROJECTS
France will provide Fr 376 million worth of concessional finance for investment in select infrastructure projects in India.

Concessional finance is presently available for water-related projects and the mining sector, but may be extended to other core sectors. The offer of concessional finance and other grants is conditional on supply of equipment from France.
This was announced at an Indo-French seminar in Delhi. The French Ambassador said the country's Prime Minister, Alain Juppe, was personally overseeing economic relations with India.
He called for an increase in the volume of Indo-French trade which currently stands at $2 billion despite a 20 percent rise last year.
SEVEN PCT GDP GROWTH TARGET IN NINTH PLAN
A seven percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) can be achieved in the ninth five-year plan (1997-2002 AD), provided the current account deficit is kept at around two percent.

This was stated by the Planning Commission. The panel stressed the need for hard decisions including a hike in the prices of petroleum products to meet the huge oil pool deficit, tapping resources from the parallel economy and a sharp increase in the tax revenue.
The tax to GDP ratio needed to be expanded from the current 10.5 percent level to 12 percent, it said. It called for increased investments in power, irrigation and rural development.

The outlay for the social sector is likely to increase by 120 billion rupees. The panel is studying the scenario in each core sector and may suggest necessary policy changes to attract $10 billion in foreign investments in the power, petroleum and telecommunications sectors.
GOLD IMPORT POLICY MAY BE LIBERALISED

The government may allow gold import under the open general licence and forward trading in bullion. This was indicated by central bank (RBI) deputy governor YV Reddy at a meeting of the World Gold Council.
He said the government was considering various issues at hand regarding the review of gold policy.
It was currently in discussions whether to liberalise the trade policy to allow select banks and corporates to import gold or allow all individuals to import gold against rupee payments.
He said the government was also considering how the import of gold could affect the balance of payments position.
The Observer
GUIDELINES FOR CORPORATE GOVERNANCE SOON
The government has asked the Industrial Development Bank of India and the Industrial Credit and Investment Council of India to suggest guidelines for corporate governance.
The two financial institutions (FIs) are likely to offer suggestions regarding their role in the different corporations and that of their nominees in the different board of directors.
This was stated by finance secretary M S Ahluwalia. He said the FIs had performed reasonably well on the boards they were present, but acted only on the basis of facts passed onto them.
They should ask for information which had a bearing on the company's affairs and influence its decisions particularly in the interest of individual shareholders, he added.
